text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Polish-Lithuanian relations are now excellent and can serve as a model to others, the countries' Presidents Aleksander Kwasniewski and Algirdas Brazauskas said at a meeting in Warsaw on Thursday.
Poland and Lithuania signed a strategic partnership treaty then.

- Poland is very likely to be accepted to Nato membership but the final decision has yet to be made and issues such as the country's stable democracy, political moderation and religious tolerance are now being closely monitored, Zbigniew Brzezinski said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Zygmunt Solorz, co-owner of private Polsat television, has not yet provided the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard with funds needed for construction of the first vessel contracted by Germany's Schoeller Holdings.
The yard expects to receive the money by the end of this week, yard board member Bogdan Oleszek said.
- British Petroleum plans to invest $500 million in petrol distribution development in Poland by 2000, BP Poland general director Krzysztof Zielicki said.
- Daewoo FSO ZTS upholstery maker in Grojec, central Poland, has formed a joint venture with South Korea's Tongheung Electric.
The join venture will carry out upholstery production for Daewoo FSO Polonez Caro and ATU Plus cars and start making upholstery for the Lanos model in the first quarter of 1997.
- The privately-owned Netia telecoms operator will cut the price of a single impulse by 0.01 zloty to 0.17 zloty on July 1, Netia's sales and marketing director Jacek Szostak said.
- The KGHM copper combine, now undergoing privatisation, will invest $800 million in new technologies, modernisation and increasing production in the next five years.
- Poland's on-line cash dispenser operators have signed an agreement allowing their customers to use over 500 cash tellers controlled by various banks.
- The state-owned Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) farming bank will issue the town of Ciechanow's five-year munibonds totalling 5.0 million zlotys.
- Bank Pekao SA will operate the consolidated bank account of Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), the state-owned telecoms monopolist, the bank said.
- Allianz BGZ insurance company has appointed Pawel Dangel president of its life and non-life insurance branches.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- The technical result of Poland's non-life insurance sector in the first quarter of 1997 was positive for the first time in years, the companies' results showed.
- The Warsaw Commodity Exchange (WGT) will shortly launch futures transactions, WGT president Wlodzimierz Rembisz said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- In the next 30 days Czech Union Banka (UB) will have to buy the 7.5 million shares of Bank Przemyslowy SA of Lodz it had agreed to buy.
If not, UB will have to pay a fine of $500,000.
PARKIET
- The listed Vistula garment maker and trader will invest 2.5 million zlotys in retail distribution in 1997, Vistula said.
- The Fameg furniture maker, controlled by National Investment Fund (NFI) Progress, is planning a share listing on the Warsaw bourse's main market in 1998.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
